claim: AGO2 loss produces a transcriptional component
supporting_evidence: whole-versus-nascent gene-effect Spearman correlation is 0.5370; some genes have positive nascent effect estimates
contradicting_or_limiting_evidence: no gene has a replicated FDR-significant AGO2 effect; robust mode classification finds no gene with jointly supported positive whole and nascent effects; single AGO2 guide and long-term CRISPRi permit indirect changes
final_judgement: compatible with, but does not establish, a transcriptional component

final_judgement: not supported as an AGO2-specific signature

claim: whole-RNA changes are attributable to one independent RNA process
supporting_evidence: composition-preserving decomposition closes numerically and assigns 186 of 520 large changes as nascent-dominant and 334 as preexisting-dominant
contradicting_or_limiting_evidence: the two components are not independent experiments; 220 of 254 large positive whole changes receive positive contributions from both components
final_judgement: mixed contributions are supported, but unique mechanistic origin is not identifiable

claim: pre-existing RNA increases prove slower degradation

final_judgement: not supported as proof of RNA stabilization

claim: nascent and pre-existing effects are independent evidence streams

claim: growth or dropout confounding is excluded

claim: AGO2 is a universal direct transcriptional repressor
supporting_evidence: whole and nascent effect estimates are moderately correlated across filtered genes
contradicting_or_limiting_evidence: no independent AGO2 guide, no donor replicate, no direct binding assay in this input, no time course, and no valid gene-level FDR resolution
final_judgement: not demonstrated by the supplied data
